item.title: Nigeria records its first Ebola case, in capital Abuja
item.description: Nigeria has reported its first known case of Ebola during Africa's latest outbreak originating in the DRC. Health Minister Muhammad Ali Pate said the patient was a woman who had recently flown to Abuja from Uganda.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Lebanon faces uncertainty as UNIFIL mandate nears end
item.description: As UN peacekeeping forces prepare to withdraw from Lebanon, Israel remains present and Hezbollah is still armed. A new EU support mission aims to strengthen Lebanon's army, but will not replace UN peacekeepers.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Sudan drone strike kills around 150 in Abyei market
item.description: A drone strike hit a market in the Abyei border region disputed by Sudan and South Sudan and killed dozens. The drone caused a large fire when it hit a fuel depot. South Sudanese officials blamed Sudan's military.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: North Korean workers treated as 'slaves' at Russian drone factory, says new report
item.description: A new report reveals the plight of North Korean workers at a drone factory in Russia. It also raised concerns that Pyongyang could gain hands-on knowledge of advanced weapons systems through the workers it sends there.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Brazil's Lula, Flavio Bolsonaro tied ahead of runoff vote
item.description: With just under a week to go before the decisive presidential runoff election, polls show left-wing incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and his right-wing challenger Flavio Bolsonaro are virtually tied.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Who are the women powering India's youth-led 'Cockroach' protests?
item.description: Facing online harassment and police detentions, women are taking to the streets of Indian cities in large numbers for the youth-led "Cockroach" protests. Amid a large-scale crackdown, they refuse to be seen as victims.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Why US investors are snapping up Germany's famed Mittelstand
item.description: Increasing amounts of US capital are flowing into Germany's traditional industrial firms and family-owned businesses. As many business owners struggle to find successors, more companies are becoming acquisition targets.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Canada: Alberta rejects separation bid, CBC projects
item.description: Voters have decisively rejected a proposal to begin the legal process toward Alberta's independence, dealing a major blow to a movement driven largely by economic grievances.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Australian MP seriously hurt in suspected car attack
item.description: Helen Haines, an independent federal lawmaker, suffered severe injuries in what Australia's prime minister has called a deliberate attack by a man in a car.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Bulgaria seeks suspects in Germany after Starlink sabotage
item.description: A Bulgarian court has issued arrest warrants for two young German nationals suspected of setting fire to Starlink antennas. The case is reminiscent of another in Poland, which Warsaw says was orchestrated by Russia.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Canada: Alberta votes on holding independence referendum
item.description: Canada's oil-rich western province of Alberta is not deemed likely to vote in favor of a real breakaway plebiscite. Nevertheless the separatist movement hopes to gain leverage over Mark Carney's government.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Can diplomacy stop another Ethiopia-Eritrea war?
item.description: Ethiopia has installed a new administration in conflict-hit Tigray after federal forces pushed back Tigrayan fighters. But tensions with Eritrea continue to raise fears of a wider regional war.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Rubio visits India with a trip to the world's largest oil refinery topping the agenda
item.description: A visit to India this week by Washington's top diplomat will skip New Delhi and instead include the world's largest oil refinery, which processes massive amounts of Russian crude. Is Trump looking for a new deal?
item.dc:subject: World
